location.section: essay on the three great essentials at the end of life (臨終三大要)

paraphrase: Three essentials for the dying: first, skilfully instruct and comfort the dying person so that right faith arises; second, let family and friends recite the Buddha's name in shifts to support the dying one's pure recollection; third, strictly avoid moving the body or weeping, lest the dying one be disturbed and lose right mindfulness.
speaker: Yinguang
notes: Recalled; exact title and wording not checked (recent).

paraphrase: Fulfil your human relations and duties, guard against evil and keep sincerity, do no evil and practise all good; truly for the sake of birth-and-death arouse the aspiration for awakening, and with deep faith and vow hold the Buddha's name.
speaker: Yinguang
